newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian stocks extend rebound from last week.
newsitem.headline: Asian stocks extend rebound from last week.

text.p: HONG KONG - Asian stock markets on Tuesday extended their recovery from a correction last week as investors took heart in an overnight surge in New York stocks.

Asian investors, fuelling a second straight day of share-price gains, read the Dow's rise as a sign that U.S. markets had shrugged off last week's negative comments by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan, brokers said.

Tokyo's Nikkei 225 index climbed 207.23 points, or 1.01 percent, to 20,810.94 in early afteroon trading while Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index took off at the opening bell and closed the morning session 169 points higher at 13,313, a gain of 1.29 percent.
Markets in Australia, Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines and Taiwan also rose.
"We are moving in line with the Dow," said Peter Lai, associate director at OCBC Securities in Hong Kong.

The Dow Jones industrial average had jumped 82 points on Monday to 6,463.94, its biggest point gain in more than a month, after finance officials downplayed Greenspan's comments about "irrational exuberance" in financial markets.

Stock markets around the world interpreted the remarks as a hint that the Fed was poised to raise interest rates to keep the U.S. market from overheating, provoking a sell-off worldwide on Friday that was partially recouped on Monday.
"For the Tokyo market, the plunge of over 650 points last week may have been a blessing in disguise, providing it with energy to bounce back," said a broker.
Australian shares were in positive territory in the afternoon although down from early Dow-inspired highs. The All Ordinaries index was 22.7 points higher at 2,362.5, a gain of 0.98 percent.
However, brokers said the bourse had been mildly disappointing with many investors still wary about Wall Street.
Secondary stocks led the Kuala Lumpur market's rise in late-morning dealings, with blue chips showing a mixed trend, traders said.
The key Composite Index was up 9.88 points to 1,213.24.
Singapore's Straits Times Industrials Index rose 14.51 points to 2,211.64 on the Dow's strength, brokers said.
"But volume is low," one dealer said. "Most markets in Asia will remain cautious."
Seoul stocks put on 5.73 points to 697.90.

Taiwan share prices also were higher but trade was slow due to a lack of any major market-inspiring news to boost buying, analysts said. The weighted index gained 32.2 points or 0.47 percent to 6,841.03.
The Philippine equities market rebounded from a 1.57 percent drop on Monday to gain back 38.22 points, or 1.24 percent, to 3,128.38 thanks to Wall Street, traders said.
Jakarta shares defied the regionwide optimism, slipping 3.7 points to 630.82, dragged down by falls in the share price of heavyweight Telkom.
The Thai stock market was closed for a holiday.
